title: 12-bar blues
summary: The most common chord progression in popular music. Learn it once, use it forever.

steps.title: The form
steps.body:
Twelve bars built from three chords: I, IV, V. In A: A7, D7, E7. The bars go:

I I I I  | IV IV I I | V IV I I (V)

The last bar is the 'turnaround' -- a V chord that pulls you back to the top of the loop. Once you can hear and play this form, you can sit in on a million songs.

steps.title: A7 (open)
steps.body: The dominant 7 chord: major triad + b7 (G). The G clashing with the C# (the 3rd) creates the tritone that gives the chord its blues 'pull'.
